headline_marked: [[Anthropic accuses Alibaba]] of illicitly distilling Claude models using 25,000 fake accounts
headline: Anthropic accuses Alibaba of illicitly distilling Claude models using 25,000 fake accounts
summary: Anthropic alleges Chinese tech giant Alibaba used 25,000 fraudulent accounts and 28.8 million exchanges to train its own AI models using Claude's output. This method, called distillation, allows competitors to build models faster and cheaper.
details: Anthropic, the American AI lab behind Claude, has formally accused Chinese tech giant Alibaba of illicitly using Claude to train its own models. This claim was made in a letter sent to the U.S. Senate, ahead of a hearing on AI issues.

The company alleges that Alibaba's effort involved 25,000 fake accounts and 28.8 million exchanges on Claude between April and June 2026. This technique, known as distillation, involves training a less advanced AI model using the output of a more sophisticated one.

Anthropic previously made similar claims against DeepSeek, Moonshot, and MiniMax, alleging 24,000 fraudulent accounts and 16 million exchanges. While distillation has legitimate uses, Anthropic argues that competing labs can exploit it to develop models at a fraction of the usual time and cost.

The American AI lab warns that such distillation campaigns could help China develop frontier AI models that rival advanced capabilities. This concern is shared by many American lawmakers, who fear China's rapid advancements in AI.

The accusation highlights the intense AI supremacy race between the U.S. and China. Both nations are implementing measures, such as export controls on hardware and rare earth materials, to gain a strategic advantage in AI development.

headline_marked: [[Elon Musk's lawsuit against OpenAI dismissed]] over statute of limitations
headline: Elon Musk's lawsuit against OpenAI dismissed over statute of limitations
summary: A federal jury in Oakland unanimously found Musk's claims were filed too late, ending the trial-level case. Musk vows to appeal, calling it a "calendar technicality."
details: A federal jury in Oakland unanimously dismissed Elon Musk's lawsuit against OpenAI, Sam Altman, Greg Brockman, and Microsoft. The nine-person advisory jury found that Musk's claims were filed outside California's three-year statute of limitations. Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers accepted the verdict, concluding the trial-level case.

Musk quickly posted on X, calling the decision a "calendar technicality" and stating he would appeal to the Ninth Circuit. OpenAI's lead counsel, William Savitt, countered that it was a "substantive decision," arguing that charitable-trust law treats donor recourse as time-bounded.

The jury's finding was narrow, focusing solely on the procedural timing. They did not rule on the merits of whether OpenAI violated its founding mission as a charitable trust. This means the core breach-of-charitable-trust theory was never substantively addressed.

The deliberation took less than two hours, a remarkably short time given three weeks of testimony from key figures like Altman, Brockman, Sutskever, and Nadella. This brevity suggests the procedural defense was clear and dispositive to the jury.

Musk's case had undergone significant attrition, starting with twenty-six claims that were whittled down over multiple pretrial stages. The two claims that reached the jury were the last survivors, ultimately dismissed on procedural grounds related to the statute of limitations.

The cumulative outcome indicates that claims with substantive legal teeth failed to advance past pretrial stages. The remaining claims were ultimately defeated by the very doctrine that gave them their initial standing: charitable-trust law's time-bound donor recourse.
